Testing for Hepatitis B For Everyone Nov. 2, 2026 Key points Getting tested for hepatitis B is the only way to find out if you are infected. All adults and pregnant women should get tested for hepatitis B. People with ongoing risk need periodic testing. You can find out if you have hepatitis B through a blood test. Why get tested Many people with hepatitis B do not look or feel sick, so testing is the only way to know if you are infected. It's important to get tested for hepatitis B, so that if you are infected you can get medical care and avoid spreading the virus to others. Chronic, or long-term, hepatitis B can cause serious health problems, including liver damage, liver cancer, liver failure, and even death. pages.text: Testing policy | Policies & legal information | W3C Skip to content Testing policy Testing helps achieve interoperability among different implementations of specifications. This document sets the testing policy that is referred to in W3C working group charters. Status: This text was copied from testing-how-to/#test-as-you-commit . A Working Group Charter may refer to this document. No substantive changes may be made to this document without a W3C Advisory Committee review of the Group Charters it is linked from. Comments should be sent as a GitHub issue . Test as you commit All normative spec changes are generally expected to have a corresponding pull request in web-platform-tests , either in the form of new tests or modifications to existing tests, or must include the rationale for why test updates are not required for the proposed update. Typically, both pull requests (spec updates and tests) will be merged at the same time. If a pull request for the specification is approved but the other needs more work, add the ' needs tests ' label or, in web-platform-tests, the ' status:needs-spec-decision ' label. Note that a test change that contradicts the specification should not be merged before the corresponding specification change. If testing is not practical due to web-platform-tests limitations, please explain why and if appropriate file an issue with the ' type:untestable ' label to follow up later. At present, 12 different data types are supported, each with 74 different argument signatures, for a total of 888 typemaps supported “out of the box”. Each of these typemaps, in turn, might require several unit tests in order to verify expected behavior for both proper and improper inputs. Currently, this results in more than 1,000 individual unit tests executed when make test is run in the numpy/tools/swig subdirectory. To facilitate this many similar unit tests, some high-level programming techniques are employed, including C and SWIG macros, as well as Python inheritance. The purpose of this document is to describe the testing infrastructure employed to verify that the numpy.i typemaps are working as expected. pages.text: Tetanus is making a comeback. There’s an easy way to fight back. | National Geographic HEALTH Tetanus is making a comeback. There’s an easy way to fight back. It's easy to dismiss, but more Americans died from tetanus last year than any year in nearly two decades. The U.S. is seeing its highest tetanus case numbers in years. Experts blame falling vaccination rates. Mark Thiessen, National Geographic By Meryl Davids Landau Published June 4, 2026 In the classic tale of tetanus, a farmworker steps on an old barn nail and develops the bacterial disease. Most Americans don’t work on farms these days, so it’s easy for people to dismiss the illness as something they’re unlikely to encounter. In reality, this serious microbial infection can impact anyone anywhere, and more Americans are succumbing. Some 38 people came down with tetanus in 2025, the highest number in nearly 20 years. Madoff’s center first pointed to the concerning trend in a report published online late last year. Tetanus: Causes and How It Spreads For Everyone Sept. 10, 2026 Español Key points Tetanus spores from the environment enter the body through cuts or wounds. Tetanus doesn't spread from person to person. It is possible to have tetanus infection more than once. Prevent tetanus by staying up to date with vaccinations and seeking appropriate care after a wound. Causes Bacteria live in the environment Spores of Clostridium tetani are common in the environment, including soil, dust, and manure. The spores develop into bacteria when they enter the body. Common exposures The spores can get into someone's body through broken skin, usually through injuries. Tetanus bacteria are more likely to infect certain breaks in the skin, including: Wounds contaminated with dirt, feces (poop), or saliva (spit) Puncture wounds (wounds caused by an object, like a nail or needle) Injuries with dead tissue (e.g., burns, crush injuries, frostbite) Dead tissue is a concern because it can promote bacteria growth. View on TensorFlow.org Run in Google Colab View source on GitHub Download notebook Overview There are 4 options for type promotion in TensorFlow. By default, TensorFlow raises errors instead of promoting types for mixed type operations. Running tf.numpy.experimental_enable_numpy_behavior() switches TensorFlow to use NumPy type promotion rules . This doc describes two new options that will be available in TensorFlow 2.15 (or currently in tf-nightly ): pip install -q tf_nightly Note: experimental_enable_numpy_behavior changes the behavior of all of TensorFlow. Setup import numpy as np import tensorflow as tf import tensorflow.experimental.numpy as tnp print ( "Using TensorFlow version %s " % tf . __version__ ) Using TensorFlow version 2.20.0 Enabling the new type promotion In order to use the JAX-like type promotion in TF-Numpy, specify either 'all' or 'safe' as the dtype conversion mode when enabling NumPy behavior for TensorFlow. This new system (with dtype_conversion_mode="all" ) is associative, commutative, and makes it easy to control what width of float you end up with (it doesn't automatically convert to wider floats). Overview SQLite Test Harness #3 (hereafter "TH3") is one of the test harnesses used for testing SQLite. TH3 meets the following objectives: TH3 is able to run on embedded platforms that lack the support infrastructure of workstations. TH3 tests SQLite in an as-deployed configuration using only published and documented interfaces. In other words, TH3 tests the compiled object code, not the source code, thus verifying that no problems were introduced by compiler bugs. "Test what you fly and fly what you test." TH3 checks SQLite's response to out-of-memory errors, disk I/O errors, and power loss during transaction commit. TH3 exercises SQLite in a variety of run-time configurations (UTF8 vs UTF16, different pages sizes, varying journal modes, etc.) TH3 achieves 100% branch test coverage (and 100% MC/DC ) over the SQLite core. (Test coverage of extensions such as FTS and RTREE is less than 100%). pages.description: Scientists call the events permafrost detachment slides. Instead of thawing from the top down, these landslides seem to originate from a weakened base

Adapted from J. M. Young et al., Geophysical Research Letters , 2026 In 2017 and 2018, a pair of strange landslides moved huge masses of rock and dirt in Canada’s Northwest Territories. The events occurred in the central Mackenzie Valley, and one of them even dammed a river and created a lake . The two natural disasters are part of a new class of landslides scientists are calling “permafrost detachment slides” in a study published in the journal Geophysical Research Letters in September. They may have been partially triggered by severe wildfires that occurred in 1995, which destabilized the ground and allowed the base of the permafrost to thaw. What’s more, these events may become more common as the planet continues to warm. “It’s a very dramatic manifestation of the changing climate,” says study co-author Joseph Young , a geoscientist who conducted the work at the University of Alberta in Canada, to Matt Simon at Grist . “They’ve only started happening in the last 10, 15 years, and it’s a very drastic and abrupt change in the landscape.” Young and his colleagues began the study after seeing something strange in the Northwest Territories in 2019. pages.text: The 10 elements of agroecology | Agroecology Knowledge Hub | Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations Share Close Agroecology Knowledge Hub The 10 Elements of Agroecology framework process The 10 Elements of Agroecology resulted from a multi-stakeholder process intended to generate a system re-design framework to be optimized and adapted to local contexts. The 10 Elements of Agroecology framework started to be developed in 2015. Prominent themes from presentations delivered during the First International Symposium on Agroecology for Food Security and Nutrition provided an initial coherent structure: recycling, efficiency, diversity, resilience and synergies as central ecological features of agroecology. Nevertheless, calls in regional meetings for reinforcing social and political aspects of agroecology were also strong. Thus, these aspects that emerged from regional consultations between 2015-2017 were clustered under an additional set of five elements: co-creation of knowledge; human and social values; culture and food traditions; responsible governance; and circular and solidarity economy. Following the refinement of element names, content, and the development of a consistent storyline highlighting the interconnected nature of agroecology and its 10 Elements, the framework was finalized after several rounds of review by international and FAO experts. The 10 Elements of Agroecology framework was launched at the Second FAO International Symposium on Agroecology held in April 2018 and continues to evolve. pages.text: The 300mph motorsport where women keep winning - BBC Sport By Jessica Abrahams BBC World Service Like "being shot out of a cannon" is the closest comparison that driver Susanne Callin can come up with for the extreme motorsport she competes in. She is a two-time European champion in Top Fuel drag racing - often described as the fastest sport on the planet. Races begin with a bone-shaking roar, as the world's fastest-accelerating cars leave the starting line, flames bursting out of their exhaust pipes. The cars surge to more than 300mph (483km/h) in races that last just four seconds, with drivers experiencing more g-force than an astronaut launching into space. It is the only elite class of motorsport where women frequently beat men to major titles. Women have won seven out of the past nine European Championships, while, until recently, female US driver Brittany Force held the world speed record in the sport. In comparison, it is 50 years since a woman even competed in a Formula 1 Grand Prix race. Women account for about 10% of participants across motorsport, and just 4% of elite drivers, according to campaign group More Than Equal. However, they made up 20% of the drivers competing in this year's US and European Top Fuel seasons. So why is this high-velocity motorsport bucking the trend? With pretty much every available television slot now exhausted, next year the Premier League and the EFL are set to hold serious discussions about its future. There are concerns, especially within non-league football, that removing the blackout could have detrimental effects on attendances and finances. Prime Minister Andy Burnham agrees, urging caution and suggesting the health of the football pyramid should come first . But many Premier League fans feel they are short-changed, locked out of many of their team's fixtures just because they live in this country. Go anywhere else in the world, and every single match is available live. With streaming so prevalent, to some the blackout feels archaic. Yet it is a complex situation, and many feel the depth of English football's pyramid is like nowhere else. BBC Sport looks at the history of the blackout, why it is unique to British football and the arguments for and against keeping it. pages.text: The 90s: Art and Fashion Exhibition Talk | Tate Britain Enjoy a one-hour introductory lecture to The 90s: Art and Fashion and then explore the exhibition at your leisure Led by a Tate Lecturer, this one hour lecture will introduce the themes and works of art in this iconic exhibition. Curated by fashion industry game-changer Edward Enninful OBE, whose lived experience of the decade informs the exhibition, The 90s: Art and Fashion examines a defining period in which a groundswell of creativity changed the face of British culture. As Britain began to emerge from recession, a new dawn of optimism, freedom, and rebellion was ushered in, epitomised by a new generation of diverse creative talent. Seen through Edward Enninful’s eyes, this sense of opportunity resulted in art, design, fashion and photography fusing into one potent cultural force, signalling an audacious renewal of British spirit. The exhibition explores how long-held hierarchies were dismantled, with high art and pop culture feeding into one another, and reflects both the energy and the challenges of the decade, looking at the enduring influence of key figures who emerged during this time. Edward Enninful OBE is one the most influential voices in fashion and culture today, bringing his perspective as curator to this exploration of the decade. The 90s: Art and Fashion is supported by McQueen. That’s the holy grail of regenerative medicine, and it has proven frustratingly elusive. When disease damages crucial organs like the heart or lungs, the best doctors can generally do is stop the harm from worsening. Now, after three decades of trial and error, the prospect of revving up the body’s own stem cells to become advanced organ repair shops is tantalizingly close. Which Code Base Should I Use To Build SQLite? SQLite is written in C. To compile SQLite, you use a C-compiler to convert the C-language source code into binary machine code. Except it is not quite that simple. The SQLite project makes a distinction between "canonical source code" and the "amalgamation". Here is what the SQLite developers mean by those terms: 1.1. Canonical Sources vs. Amalgamation Canonical Source Code or Canonical Sources → The canonical source code is the urtext for SQLite. These are the source code files that are typed in and maintained by the SQLite developers and that are stored under the source code management system. If you pull a copy of the SQLite source code from its Fossil repository ( https://sqlite.org/src ) or from the GitHub mirror ( https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite ), you get the canonical source code. Amalgamation → As part of the build process for SQLite, the canonical source code files get transformed and concatenated together into a few big C-language code files: sqlite3.c sqlite3.h shell.c These " amalgamation " source files are also C-code. Combining lots of smaller code files together into a few big C-code files makes SQLite easier to compile. And it helps the C-compiler optimize the code so that it runs faster. Learn about other national symbols. History of the American flag The flag of the United States is a symbol of freedom before which Americans recite the pledge of allegiance . The flag's 13 red and white stripes represent the 13 original colonies. Its 50 white stars on a blue background represent the 50 states. Each of the colors on the flag has a meaning: Red: valor and bravery White: purity and innocence Blue: vigilance, perseverance, and justice A star is added to the flag when a new state joins the United States. The flag was last modified on July 4, 1960, when Hawaii was incorporated as a state. Learn more about the evolution of the American flag and its earlier designs. How to raise the flag Follow these guidelines to properly display the American flag [PDF, 162KB]. It is a fascinating natural and cultural landscape adapted to extreme conditions. Alaska has the only Arctic parks in the National Park System, and together, those parks make up more than a quarter of the total amount of land managed by the National Park Service. The boundary of the Arctic is the Arctic Circle, an imaginary line around the Earth (at about 66.5° North Latitude) where, for at least one day each year, the sun does not completely set (June 21) or rise (December 22). pages.text: The Army's Vision and Strategy | The United States Army Who We Are The Army's Vision and Strategy OUR MISSION Our purpose remains constant "This We'll Defend" has been our Army's motto since the Revolutionary War. It reminds us that our purpose is timeless and clear: to fight and win our Nation's wars. When our Army hits the dirt, America means business. Our teammates don't want to fight without us, and our enemies are wise to fear us. We are not a Pacific Army or a Europe Army. We are not Brigade-centric or Division-centric. We are a global force that fights when called upon at the scale required. THIS WE'LL DEFEND When you are downrange and you hear a call sign come over the net, a mental picture comes to mind... When the American Army comes over the net, we want our teammates to know that the best, most disciplined land force in the world has arrived. All of us contribute to that reputation. We are proud of this team. When we are called, we will answer... and we will win. This We'll Defend! pages.text: The Artisans Trying to Bring Back Neolithic Fashion | National Geographic Premium HISTORY & CULTURE The Artisans Trying to Bring Back Neolithic Fashion A growing community of craftspeople are trying to build knowledge of ancient clothing—by making it themselves. Historical craft specialist Vasi Birchwood recreates fashion from the Neolithic period on her Youtube channel. This outfit is one of her creations. The jacket is made of deer skin, stitched with deer skin cord and a bone awl, and adorned with moose teeth. The shirt underneath the jacket is made of undyed linen, hand stitched with linen thread. The skirt is made of deer skin and decorated with braided hemp strings. Photo Illustration: NGM Staff; Source Photos for Illustration: Vasi Birchwood By Starre Vartan Published November 2, 2026 Around the fire, no one seems especially bothered by the rain. Some people duck beneath bark shelters to continue twisting cordage from plant fibers. Others cook foraged plants or work leather while steam rises from damp clothing. A few wander into the drizzle to gather more wood before returning to the warmth of the flames. Among them is historical craft specialist and YouTube educator Vasi Birchwood . For Birchwood, weather isn't an inconvenience so much as another participant in this meeting of experiential archeologists and craft experts in Northern Germany. pages.text: The Astronomical Problem of Space Junk Skip to main content Illustration by Emily Lankiewicz / Images by Samantha Lawler / NASA / smspsy via Adobe Stock and public domain We have launched all manner of satellite and machinery into low-Earth orbit. But what goes up must come down. Most often, these items burn up in the atmosphere upon re-entry, which isn’t good for air quality or the ozone layer. But not everything incinerates — and increasing amounts of debris are hurtling back toward Earth and landing in backyards and farm fields. Falling detritus disrupts air travel and risks collision with infrastructure and people on the ground. There are those who argue that additional regulation is required around the launching and de-orbiting of these materials. In this episode, host Ari Daniel speaks with astronomer Samantha Lawler and Smithsonian contributing writer Dan Falk about space junk and the concern among researchers that it is becoming a growing threat to public safety. Overview The base64() function is an SQL function implemented as a loadable extension for SQLite. The function converts a binary BLOB into equivalent RFC 4648 text or converts RFC 4648 text into the equivalent BLOB. The base64() function is not a standard part of SQLite. It must be loaded as a separate extension. The source code to base64() is in the base64.c source file in the ext/misc/ folder of the SQLite source tree. The base64() function is not included in standard builds of the SQLite library, but it is loaded by default in the CLI . This is typical of the CLI which loads various extensions above and beyond what are available in the standard SQLite library. 2. Features The base64() function always takes a single argument. If the argument to base64() is a BLOB, then the return value is TEXT that is the RFC 4648 encoding of that BLOB. If the argument to base64() is base64 TEXT then the return value is a BLOB that is the binary data corresponding to that base64 TEXT. If the argument to base64() is NULL, then NULL is returned. An error is raised if the argument to base64() is something other than TEXT, BLOB, or NULL. If the argument is TEXT, leading and trailing whitespace is ignored. The continent of North America has been inhabited by humans for at least 16,500 years. As early as the 1500s, early settlers and European thinkers were interested in discovering how humans had come to populate North and South America. One theory suggested the migration of Norsemen across Greenland into North America. Another theory proposed the island of Atlantis as the origins of human life in the New World. Yet another idea proposed that the inhabitants had generated out of mud. However, by the early 1800s, scientists and theorists began discussing the possibility of a land bridge that had spanned between Asia and North America thousands of years ago. For all of human history people have looked up to the inky blackness of night and marvelled at the stars. Yet true darkness just isn’t something Europeans experience in the same way anymore due to artificial light illuminating the night sky. Light pollution can disrupt sleep and circadian rhythms, affect wildlife and ecosystems, and contribute to unnecessary energy use and carbon emissions. With this in mind, it’s no surprise more of us than ever are swapping chasing the sun for chasing the stars instead. DarkSky International is a non-profit organisation that certifies destinations around the world for the quality of their night skies, their approach to artificial lighting, conservation efforts and long-term commitment to protecting darkness. Ana Lui Photography By Lauren Gamp and Orla Thomas Published August 31, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). The largest of Spain’s Balearics, Majorca has a hotel scene as diverse as the island itself. In the capital city of Palma, you’ll find stylish crash pads and converted palaces, while the peaceful interior — home to charming hilltop villages and the Serra de Tramuntana mountain range — is the place to experience hospitality rooted in the land. Wherever you stay, you’ll never be far from the calas (coves) of the Mediterranean coast, ideal for lazy beach days and lingering seaside lunches. Can Ferrereta Best for: art and design Hidden down a side street in the southeastern market town of Santanyi, this property reveals its lustre by degrees. First, the original stone floor and elegant archways of the 17th-century mansion house are on show in the lobby; next, a library stocked with Assouline coffeetable books and vinyl. In the garden beyond, a 25-metre pool sparkles in the sunlight and, under a nearby nasturtium-trailed pergola, diners enjoy zesty salads and jamón croquetas.
